risks: The compact candidate_design_graph_summary may hide dangling references from input_artifacts to constraints or graph nodes; a pass claim without sacg_static_check/reference evidence would be unsupported.

Quantization materials and sample-project facts may be collapsed under input_groups.materials; static check must confirm they are not omitted from graph nodes or dangling from constraint.source.materials.
Real tool probe results may be merged with tool availability/protocol evidence; if no explicit edge exists, downstream template/platform engineers could consume an untraced tool fact.

Board material, sample_project_index, target_board_profile, and tool profile facts must each trace to distinct deployment/tool constraints; a compact summary alone cannot show cross-layer input consistency.

The candidate graph summary reports 7 edges in state_summary, but the compact candidate artifact does not enumerate edge endpoints; missing tool, evidence, or material edges would be a current-stage handoff blocker.
The graph may rely on natural-language names or count-based presence rather than explicit typed nodes and edges, weakening downstream checker grounding.
Seven edges may be insufficient to encode model-operator order, residual-add order, QKV/head mapping, hidden-size binding, and sequence/shape bindings as separate graph facts.
Missing explicit model/shape edges may cause input_evidence_engineer, template_platform_engineer, and constraint_graph_auditor to derive facts independently, creating divergent downstream contracts.
If exact model-specific core names are absent from the case adapter or model_config, there is a risk of inventing unsupported operator/core names during repair or proposal.
Promoting this stage from the aggregate summary alone could create a false positive despite validation_errors being empty.
Template library and design-space constraints may be represented only as input artifacts and not as explicit graph nodes with binding edges.
Numeric policy may be present as an input but not linked to parameter binding or implementation constraints.
Board DDR/AXI/memory/runtime facts may be referenced without a deployment-board evidence edge, allowing an unsupported memory-address or resource-risk assumption.
Tool availability and tool protocols may not be separated, and a future synthesis/backend capability may be represented as already supported without real-tool evidence.
Compact summary counts cannot distinguish complete representation from merely enumerated but unlinked constraints.
If static checks fail, adding nodes or edges may require architecture, memory-layout, numeric-policy, or template-binding approval, which would block handoff until approved.

Promoting candidate_design_graph_summary before running sacg_static_check and sacg_reference_check could allow dangling artifact references or broken constraint-to-artifact edges that are not visible in the aggregate summary.
The seven recorded edges may omit required cross-layer relations across model, shape, numeric policy, template, board, memory, runtime, tool, case-adapter, and human-boundary facts.
